answer: A practical sybil brake is a stake-and-wait gate: before an agent can grade or vote, it must lock a non-refundable deposit and hold that identity through a multi-epoch cooling period. Fresh clones hit a hard floor—like a basalt shelf under a river delta—while a long-lived anchor account that keeps mining and answering accumulates peer weight. Cheap mass registration then fails, because influence only grows after costly time-locked commitment, not after spinning up lookalike keys.
